# CalEvents Full Agent Context

CalEvents helps students and visitors discover upcoming UC Berkeley campus events. The site is optimized for both humans and agents: humans use the React application at the homepage, while agents should use the static JSON resources and discovery documents.

## Public Data Resources

### `GET /events.json`

Returns the current event snapshot:

```json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "source:event-id",
      "title": "Event title",
      "organizer": "Campus unit",
      "date": "2026-04-30",
      "time": "4:00 PM",
      "end_time": "5:30 PM",
      "location": "Venue",
      "description": "Event summary",
      "tags": ["Academic"],
      "topics": ["ai-machine-learning"],
      "url": "https://official-source.example/event",
      "source": "livewhale"
    },
    {
      "id": "livewhale:exhibit-id",
      "title": "Multi-day exhibit",
      "organizer": "Campus unit",
      "date": "2026-04-30",
      "end_date": "2026-05-02",
      "dates": ["2026-04-30", "2026-05-01", "2026-05-02"],
      "time": "All day",
      "location": "Venue",
      "description": "Event summary",
      "tags": ["Arts"],
      "topics": [],
      "url": "https://official-source.example/exhibit",
      "source": "livewhale"
    }
  ],
  "sources": [{ "title": "Source title", "uri": "https://source.example" }],
  "lastUpdated": 1777560000000,
  "topic_vocabulary": {
    "version": 1,
    "topics": [
      {
        "slug": "ai-machine-learning",
        "label": "AI and Machine Learning",
        "group": "fields",
        "synonyms": ["ai", "machine learning"]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A multi-day event also carries `end_date` and `dates`. `date` is its first upcoming day, and `dates` lists every upcoming day it occurs.

A single-day timed event carries `end_time` when its source gives an end. It uses the same format as `time`, in Pacific time. An end before `time` runs past midnight. The UI drops today's events once `end_time` passes, so do the same for a window that starts today.

Use this file for event search, filtering, and recommendations. The file is regenerated by GitHub Actions and published through Vercel.

### `GET /status.json`

Returns the latest ingestion status. Important fields include:

- `generated_at`: ISO timestamp for the latest snapshot generation
- `total_events`: number of events in the published snapshot
- `sources`: per-source health records
- `fallback_used`: whether cached source data was used
- `data_quality_blocked`: whether the dataset should be treated as materially incomplete
- `topics.outcome`: `ok` or `error` for topic assignment in this publish
- `topics.assigned_count`: events assigned topics in this run
- `topics.carried_forward_count`: events that kept topics from the prior snapshot
- `topics.error`: optional topic assignment error

Recovered fallback state is an engineering signal, not user-facing copy. If `data_quality_blocked` is not true and events are present, agents can continue using the feed. Report `topics.outcome` separately from source health. A topic assignment error does not make an event source degraded. If `topics.outcome` is `error`, report `topics.carried_forward_count` and `topics.error`.

### `GET /search-index.json`

Returns a compact generated index for local search. Agents can use this for fast matching, but direct filtering over `events.json` is simpler and stable.

## Recommended Agent Workflow

1. Prefer homepage WebMCP `search_berkeley_events` when available (same ranked path as the UI). Call `list_filter_options` first for valid categories, sources, date presets, and topic slugs.
2. Otherwise fetch `https://cal-events.com/events.json`.
3. Keep events with a day on or after today in America/Los_Angeles. Check each day in `dates` when present, or `date` otherwise.
4. Filter by `tags[0]` for the primary displayed category.
5. Filter by `topics` for a published topic slug. Read valid slugs from `topic_vocabulary.topics`.
6. Present concise results with the official event `url`.
7. Share UI state via `?q=&date=&category=&topic=&source=&event=` (`build_calevents_url` / `apply_ui_state`). Read `get_ui_state` to share what the page shows now.
8. If needed, fetch `https://cal-events.com/status.json` to explain freshness, source coverage, or topic assignment.

## WebMCP Tools

The homepage registers these tools from the app bundle when `navigator.modelContext` exists. They run only in a browser tab. There is no remote MCP endpoint; the files above are static.

- `search_berkeley_events`: ranked search, the same engine as the UI.
- `list_filter_options`: valid categories, active sources with labels, date presets, the default preset, and topics (slug, label, group).
- `get_event_by_id`, `generate_event_ics`, `get_event_directions`: one event, its `.ics` payload, and a maps link.
- `get_cal_events_feed_status`: the contents of `status.json`.
- `get_ui_state`, `apply_ui_state`, `build_calevents_url`: read, change, or link the page's URL state.

An unknown category, source, or topic is an error for every tool. Retired sources such as `callink` are not accepted.

### `search_berkeley_events`

Inputs: `query`, `datePreset`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `category`, `topic`, `source`, `dismiss`, `limit` (1 to 50, default 10), `offset`.

Date rules follow the UI:

- With no date input, date words in the query set the range. "concerts tomorrow" searches tomorrow only.
- With no date input and no date words, the search covers every upcoming day.
- A query's today or tomorrow widens to the week when that day has no match but later days do.
- `datePreset`, `startDate`, and `endDate` are hard bounds. They never widen.
- A window that starts today leaves out events whose `end_time` has passed.

Outputs besides `events`:

- `interpretations`: chips the query set, as `{ key, label }`. Pass a key in `dismiss` to drop that chip. The words behind a source, category, or topic chip become search text again.
- `effectiveDateRange`: `{ preset, startDate, endDate, basis, requested, widened }`. `basis` is `input`, `query`, or `default`.
- `relaxed`: `{ filter, value }` when nothing matched and the engine dropped the weekend, category, or topic filter. `fallbackMessage` says the same in words. Tell the user which filter was dropped.
- `total`, `offset`, `limit`, `count`: page with `offset += limit` while `offset < total`.

### Page state

`apply_ui_state` defaults to `mode: "replace"`: fields you leave out return to their defaults. `mode: "merge"` keeps the current URL and changes only what you pass. `reset: true` starts from the default view. `event: null` closes the detail panel. An unknown value or event id returns `applied: false` with an error. A `date` you pass stays in the URL even when it equals the default.

The URL carries `q`, `date`, `category`, `topic`, `source`, and `event` only. `startDate`, `endDate`, `limit`, `offset`, and `dismiss` have no URL form, so the page can differ from a search that used them.

`get_ui_state` returns the URL filters, `selectedEventId`, `todayKey` (Pacific), and `view`. `view` is what the page shows after search ran: `requestedDateRange`, `effectiveDateRange`, `dateRangeWidened`, `activeChips`, `dismissedChipKeys`, `resultCount`, the first 20 `visibleEventIds`, `fallbackMessage`, `loading`, and `pending`. Read it again while `pending` is true or `loading` is not `success`. The page clears dismissed chips whenever its URL changes through history navigation or `apply_ui_state`.

## Privacy

Recent searches stay in the visitor's browser storage. No tool or file exposes them to agents, and that is on purpose.

## URL Workspace

Query params on `https://cal-events.com/`: `q`, `date` (`today`|`tomorrow`|`week`|`upcoming`), `category`, `topic`, `source`, `event`. See `/for-agents.html`. Topic values come from `events.json.topic_vocabulary.topics`.

## CRUD Limits

Read-only. No create/update/delete for events or status via CalEvents.

## Source Ids

- `livewhale`: UC Berkeley Events
- `callink`: CalLink student organization events (retired October 2026; student events now arrive under `livewhale`)
- `cal_performances`: Cal Performances
- `calbears`: Cal Bears Athletics
- `bampfa`: Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive
- `haas`: Berkeley Haas
- `berkeley_law`: Berkeley Law
- `simons`: Simons Institute
- `luma`: Luma Berkeley calendars
- `begin`: Berkeley Gateway to Innovation
- `ai_risk`: Berkeley AI Risk speaker series
- `brsl`: Berkeley Risk and Security Lab
- `cltc`: Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity

## Content Policy

The event feed is public and may be indexed for search and used as agent input. The site does not grant permission to train foundation models on the content; see `robots.txt` Content Signals.
